For patients with limb-threatening ischemia and limited venous material, particularly those who are not good candidates for more extensive procedures like a femorocrural bypass or amputation, semi-closed endarterectomy (SCDE) of the superficial femoral artery combined with a short popliteo-crural bypass is considered an acceptable alternative. This approach provides relief from limb ischemia by restoring blood flow to the affected limb.

The combination of SCDE and short popliteo-crural bypass offers good results, as demonstrated in multiple studies, including those mentioned in your dataset. These procedures can help restore normal blood flow to the leg, alleviating pain and improving overall function for many patients.

It is essential to note that while SCDE combined with a short popliteo-crural bypass can be an acceptable alternative, it's crucial to consider individual patient factors, such as overall health, comorbid conditions, and specific medical history. Your healthcare provider will assess your suitability for this procedure based on a comprehensive evaluation of your condition.

In summary, semi-closed endarterectomy combined with short venous bypass in the case of insufficient venous material can be considered an acceptable alternative for limb-threatening ischemia when other options are not feasible due to limited venous material.
